prompt:
You are auditing how an English sentence can be read. Below are a SENTENCE and, inside it, one DEMAND: a modal word (shall, should, must, may, can, has the right to, or their negations) and the acts it applies to; BEARER names who or what the demand is on. List every reading of the DEMAND that a careful reader of this English could take. Readings differ when they require, forbid or permit different things: for example each joined act on its own, or only the acts done together, or any one of several ways at the bearer's choice; or a modifier or phrase applying to one of the joined acts, or to all of them. Count readings that differ only in wording as one. Do not list a reading this English does not support. Use only the text below; do not use tools or outside knowledge. Answer only with the readings, one per line, numbered `1.`, `2.`, ..., each a plain-English sentence saying what is required, forbidden or permitted.

SENTENCE: 4. Everyone has the right to form and to join trade unions for the protection of his interests.
DEMAND: Everyone has the right to form and to join trade unions for the protection of his interests
BEARER: everyone

cli.result:
1. Everyone is permitted to form trade unions, and separately is permitted to join trade unions, in each case for the protection of his interests. Each right stands on its own, so a person may do either one without the other.
2. Everyone is permitted to form trade unions and to join trade unions without any condition. "For the protection of his interests" only explains why the right exists and does not limit when it applies.
3. Everyone is permitted to form trade unions without condition, and is permitted to join trade unions for the protection of his interests. The purpose phrase limits only the right to join.
4. Everyone is permitted to form or join only those trade unions that exist to protect workers' interests. The phrase describes the kind of union, not the person's reason for acting.
